study_identification.author_journal_year: Sampaio et al., Artificial Intelligence In Medicine, 2025
study_identification.title: A generalizable normative deep autoencoder for brain morphological anomaly detection: application to the multi-site StratiBip dataset on bipolar disorder in an external validation framework

study_characteristics.study_objective: To develop a generalizable multivariate normative modelling framework for characterizing brain morphology, applied to bipolar disorder (BD), using deep autoencoders in an anomaly detection framework, combined with a confounder removal step that integrates training and external validation.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Visual quality check of T1-weighted images. CAT12-based quality check by verifying the spatial registration across images and identifying images with an intensity covariance below two standard deviations.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: M-ComBat harmonization was used to remove site effects. The HCP-YA dataset was used as the reference site. The model was fitted exclusively on a normative sample (HCP-YA) and later applied to all test data (StratiBip).

response_variable.answer: Cortical thickness (68 ROIs); Gray matter volume (50 ROIs); White matter volume (52 ROIs)

predictor_effects.answer: The LR coefficient estimations were performed exclusively on the HCP-YA training set, and the estimated effects were removed from both HCP-YA training set and StratiBip test set.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study explicitly addresses nuisance variables (site effects, age, sex, TIV) and uses a confounder removal pipeline (M-ComBat and linear regression) to handle them.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: In this study, we present a framework for the harmonization of external test sets, i.e., data collected in sites differing from the training set. Site effects, arising from inter-site differences in MRI scanners and acquisition protocols, encode latent information that makes data not directly comparable, mask biological effects of interest, and, most importantly, are easily learnable for ML models, potentially confounding these analyses [43]. To address this, we developed a pipeline to harmonize brain features from the multi-site StratiBip external test set with the HCP-YA training set. This step was aimed to remove both intratest set and inter-dataset differences, enabling the reliable application of the trained AE normative model in an EV framework. The pipeline was based on the ComBat (Combatting Batch Effects) tool, described below. After data harmonization, we proceeded with the removal of variance associated with age and sex biocovariates from regional volumes and CT features, and harmonized TIV from volume features, via standard LR [51,52].

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model was trained and validated using a 10-fold cross-validation on the HCP-YA training set.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The number of layers, the number of neurons, the batch size, the number of epochs, the learning rate and the l2 norm coefficient were optimized in a 10 fold CV hyperparameter tunning process with a random search strategy as detailed in the supplementary information. After hyperparameter tunning, the best AE model was re-trained on the entire HCPYA training set.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not use a separate independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The model was validated on the external multi-site StratiBip dataset.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: We applied the trained normative AE model to the external StratiBip test set.

deviation_metric.answer: Reconstruction Error (RE); Mean Deviation Score (MDS); modified Z-score (mZ)

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Mann-Whitney U (MWU) test to compare RE distributions between HC and BD. ROC curve analysis to evaluate MDS-based discrimination. Pairwise feature RE absolute differences to compute heterogeneity. Block maxima approach to investigate extreme value statistics.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Brain deviating scores were greater, more heterogeneous, and with increased extreme values in the BD group, with volumes prominently from the basal ganglia, hippocampus, and adjacent regions emerging as significantly deviating.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The BD group showed a significantly higher MDS median (0.2264) compared to the HC group (0.1988). Higher BD deviations were found in CT in the right inferior temporal gyrus, and in volumes of subcortical and adjacent regions belonging to the cerebellum and the limbic system (hippocampus, striatum, globus pallidus). RE patterns were more homogeneous in the HC group. The BD group was characterized by a more pronounced extreme value profile. The AUC-ROC for discriminating BD vs. HC was 0.6129.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study did not account for medication effects on BD or comorbidities. The linear regression might not fully capture non-linear biological effects. The uncertainty of MRI-based features was not thoroughly evaluated. The AE-based network is a black-box model, and the RE lacks directionality. The evaluation of false-positive deviations is limited. The dataset only included young adults.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study proposes a generalizable end-to-end pipeline for brain morphological multivariate normative modelling and personalized anomaly detection based on deep AEs, with a novel CR step that enabled the effective translation of the model to external datasets.

general_notes.general_notes: The study provides a custom python class 'neuro-combat_pyClasse' for M-ComBat harmonization, compatible with sklearn Pipelines.
